pageCache.pageTitle: British Values and Protected Characteristics - Willowbrook Primary School
pageCache.text:
British Values and Protected Characteristics
British Values
At Willowbrook Primary School we aim to prepare children for life in modern Britain by ensuring that the fundamental British Values are introduced, discussed, and lived out through the ethos and work of the school.
Our school values are linked and unpinned by British Values:
School Assemblies as well as RE lessons enhance the children’s learning opportunities and encourage both the British Values and our School Values to be enacted.
In addition, we use Jigsaw PSHE which helps promote the fundamental British Values of Democracy, The rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs. Jigsaw contributes, as a good PSHE programme should, to the British Values agenda very significantly, both through the direct teaching of information and through the experiential learning children will enjoy.
Democracy Rule of law
Individual liberty
Mutual Respect
Tolerance of different cultures and religions
Protected Characteristics
As well as the British Values, and our Willowbrook Rappers Values, we are committed to Equalities Education. We work to ensure that our children understand that:
The Equality Act became law in 2010. It covers everyone in Britain and protects people from discrimination, harassment and victimisation - everyone in Britain is protected. This is because the Equality Act protects people against discrimination because of the protected characteristics that we all have. Under the Equality Act, there are nine Protected Characteristics:
At Willowbrook, we teach and promote these in our curriculum and embed them into our ethos. Our vision and values, enable us to ensure children understand and show the care, acceptance and tolerance to all we expect.
The document below outlines our whole-school approach to the Protected Characteristics we uphold.
Willowbrook's Approach to Protected Characteristics
To read more about how our curriculum links to both British Values and Protected Chacrteristics please see our curriculum documents here.
Everyone is different
We celebrate our differences
We are all equal in our differences
Disability
Gender reassignment
Religion or belief
Marriage or civil partnership
Sexual orientation
Pregnancy and maternity

pageCache.text:
Ethos and Values
Willowbrook Primary School is a warm and welcoming community where children and adults flourish through love, laughter and learning.
We know every child as an individual and aim to offer a safe environment that fosters positivity, empathy and resilience. We develop respectful relationships, and skills and create a thirst for learning. Children can expect to work with staff who care about them and strive to provide for their development to ensure that they flourish personally and academically with a sense of pride. Our aim for every child is to gain the confidence, knowledge and skills to achieve their potential.
Our values of respect, kindness and ambition are interwoven into our daily routines.

Ethos and Values

Welcome
Welcome to Willowbrook Primary School. It is my pleasure and privilege to be Head of this small school set in the heart of Trowbridge.
We are a caring, inclusive school where children are at the heart of everything we do. At Willowbrook, we actively promote the values of respect, kindness and ambition, and these guide our learning, behaviour and relationships every day.
At Willowbrook Primary School, our ethos is rooted in the belief that we flourish together through love, laughter and learning. These principles shape our daily interactions, our learning environment and the opportunities we provide for every child. We are proud to be building a strong and supportive community where high expectations for all sit alongside genuine opportunities for all. Every child is encouraged to believe in themselves, to take pride in their achievements and to aim high, whatever their starting point.
We work closely with families to ensure our children feel safe, valued and inspired to learn. Together, we are nurturing confident learners who are well prepared for the future.
You are warmly welcome to visit. If you have any questions or would like to view our school, please do not hesitate to get in touch with us. I am always happy to talk to parents about any aspect of their children’s education.
I look forward to meeting you.
Lindsay Hann Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Wonderful Science - News - Willowbrook Primary School
pageCache.text:
Wonderful Science
As part of their science learning about states of matter, Year 3/4 children made oobleck by mixing cornflour and water. This exciting investigation helped them explore how materials can behave in different ways. The children observed that oobleck acts like both a liquid and a solid: when it is poured, it flows like a liquid, but when pressure is applied, it feels hard like a solid. This hands-on activity helped deepen their understanding of solids and liquids while developing their enquiry and observation skills.

pageCache.pageTitle: Modern Foreign Languages (MFL) - Willowbrook Primary School
pageCache.text:
Modern Foreign Languages (MFL)
Intent
At Willowbrook Primary School, we use the Language Angels scheme of work and resources to ensure we offer a relevant, broad, vibrant and ambitious foreign languages curriculum that will inspire and excite our pupils using a wide variety of topics and themes.
All pupils will be expected to achieve their full potential by encouraging high expectations and excellent standards in their foreign language learning - the ultimate aim being that pupils will feel willing and able to continue studying languages beyond Key Stage 2.
The four key language learning skills; listening, speaking, reading and writing will be taught and all necessary grammar will be covered in an age-appropriate way across the primary phase. This will enable pupils to use and apply their learning in a variety of contexts, laying down solid foundations for future language learning and also helping the children improve overall attainment in other subject areas. In addition, the children will be taught how to look up and research language they are unsure of and they will have a bank of reference materials to help them with their spoken and written tasks going forward.
The intent is that all pupils will develop a genuine interest and positive curiosity about foreign languages, finding them enjoyable and stimulating. Learning a second language will also offer pupils the opportunity to explore relationships between language and identity, develop a deeper understanding of other cultures and the world around them with a better awareness of self, others and cultural differences. The intention is that they will be working towards becoming life-long language learners.
Implementation
We follow the National Curriculum for MFL and the children in KS2 progressively develop skills in French through well-planned lessons using the Language Angels Scheme of Work. French is taught weekly to children from Year 3, and lessons are focused on developing the four key language learning skills; listening, speaking, reading and writing.
Our children learn French through active participation in actions, rhymes, stories, song, grammar focus, video clips, sentence structure, dictionary work and may other creative ways to extend, embed and combine language skills.
As well as each subsequent lesson within a unit being progressive, units increase in level of challenge, stretch and linguistic and grammatical complexity. Children in Year 3 begin learning French and then their skills, knowledge and understanding progress throughout their time in KS2. The units of work contain progressively more challenging activities and lessons will have more content as the children become more confident and ambitious with the foreign language they are learning. Lessons offering appropriate levels of challenge are taught at all times to ensure children learn effectively, continuously building their knowledge of, and enthusiasm for, the language they are learning.
Pupils will continuously build on their previous knowledge as they progress in their French language learning journey through the primary phase. Previous language will be recycled, revised, recalled and consolidated whenever possible and appropriate.
Impact
Children at Willowbrook are encouraged to understand the relevance of what they are learning in languages and how it relates to everyday life, work and travel. It is emphasised how the language could help them in another country or to talk to a French speaker, both now and in their future careers. Teachers foster an enjoyment of languages through a variety of lessons including interactive, singing and outdoor lessons. Progression through a topic should be evident in the development of key skills and acquisition of main vocabulary. Each term, in the final session, the children complete some low-stakes assessment activities to inform future planning and retrieval activities. Evidence is kept of children’s work in knowledge organiser booklets. French is monitored by the subject leader throughout all year groups in Key Stage 2 using a variety of strategies such as book scrutinises, lesson observations, staff discussions and pupil questionnaires. Feedback is then given to teachers at staff meetings and we reflect on the subject and pupil progress frequently as a team.

pageCache.pageTitle: VE Day Anniversary - News - Willowbrook Primary School
pageCache.text:
VE Day Anniversary
On Thursday, we marked the 80th anniversary of VE Day with a joyful celebration filled with music, games, and delicious cake. The school community came together to honour this historic occasion, enjoying traditional songs and a lively party atmosphere. Children took part in a range of fun activities, creating a heartwarming sense of togetherness across the school.
A huge thank you to our wonderful PTFA for organising such a memorable event and for providing the fantastic refreshments. It was a truly special day for everyone involved!

Wraparound Care
We are thrilled to announce the launch of our new wraparound care provision at Willowbrook Primary School, starting from 24th February 2025.
Our wraparound care will offer a safe, engaging, and fun environment where your children can learn, play, and unwind before and after school.
Breakfast Club
Hours: 8.00am – 8:45am
Cost: £3 per session
We provide an breakfast with a variety of healthy options, including cereal, toast, pastries, fruit juice, fruit, and yoghurts.
After School Care
Hours: 3:15pm – 4.15pm
Cost: £2 per session until 4:15pm (including a drink and snack)
Options include: Choose between a 'chill out' club (featuring puzzles, board games, balance bikes, scooters, iPads and reading materials) or one of our scheduled activities (including dance, football, netball, rugby and gymnastics) led by a member of school staff or an Active Trowbridge sports coach.
Why Choose Us?
Looking for a place where your child can have fun, learn, and unwind? Our wraparound care offers a warm and welcoming space with exciting activities tailored to suit all interests. Whether they want to get creative, burn off energy outdoors, or just relax with friends, there's something for everyone! Plus, with flexible hours and affordable pricing, it’s the perfect solution for busy families!
How to Register
All bookings to be made via ParentMail at least 24 hours in advance.

We look forward to welcoming your children to our wraparound care program!

Physical Education (PE)
Intent
Here a Willowbrook we believe that PE is a vital part of educating the whole child, ensuring that they have the skills, knowledge and understanding to lead a healthy life now and in the future.
We believe that PE provides children with the opportunity to learn about physiology, health, well-being, relationships and personal goals and challenges. This could be within competitive sports, PE lessons, fitness activities or a range of other outdoor activities.
We aim to provide a PE curriculum that children from EYFS to Year 6 enjoy and fully participate in but which also allows them to experience a wide range of activities that help them to develop their health, fitness and wellbeing. We intend to offer a high-quality physical education curriculum that inspires all children to succeed and excel in competitive sport and other physically demanding activities. It provides opportunities for children to become physically confident in a way which supports their health and fitness. Opportunities to compete in sport and other activities build character and help to embed values such as fairness, teamwork, resilience and respect.
At Willowbrook we recognise that children come to PE with a range of experiences and abilities and make sure that all children are fully supported within PE whatever their needs medical, physical, SEND or well-being. PE at Willowbrook is fully inclusive and recognises and supports everyone.
Implementation
Staff teaching PE, which includes Active Trowbridge coaches, will plan and teach PE lessons using our PE scheme of work. The PE programme provides fun and simple to follow activities for Early Years Foundation Stage, Key Stage 1 and Key Stage 2 that give children the confidence and skills required for later life.
It is fully aligned to the proposed National Curriculum and Ofsted requirements and focuses on the development of agility, balance and coordination, healthy competition and cooperative learning. The foundations of the Schemes are based on Fundamental Movement Skills (FMS) of agility, balance and coordination, inclusive competition and broader essential holistic skills (creative, cognitive, social and personal skills).
Impact
Willowbrook pupils should demonstrate confidence in a broad range of PE and sporting skills, evident in lessons and also (for many) in participation in inter-schools and external events. Success in PE should also be evident in their social and personal skills, resilience and sense of teamwork.

Religious Education (RE)
Intent
The National Association of Teachers of Religious Education (NATRE) state: “learning in RE helps to underpin the development of respect and tolerance and supports school values and the preparation of pupils for life in modern Britain.”
Willowbrook’s intent is for our pupils to gain knowledge and understanding of different religions and cultures, and an empathy with people and their beliefs. Using the RE Today scheme we are developing children’s critical thinking skills and increasing their motivation to learn about different religions. The knowledge gained from the study of world religions, and the reflection and evaluation they will take part in, will increase their respect and acceptance of those from diverse cultures and beliefs. The RE Today scheme, which is tailored to suit each class, whilst maintaining fidelity to the scheme, allows RE to “contribute to children’s education in schools by provoking challenging questions about meaning and purpose in life, beliefs about God, ultimate reality, issues of right and wrong and what it means to be human.” (RE TODAY Website).
The essence of RE in EYFS is to develop their curiosity, questioning and spirituality. We aim to enable the children to gain knowledge, skills and experience that supports their on-going development in religious education. RE in EYFS can add to all the areas of learning but particularly self-confidence and self-awareness and understanding the world – people and communities and the world.
Implementation
Religious Education is a statutory subject of the curriculum for all pupils in each year group and ‘should be provided for all registered pupils except those withdrawn at the request of their parents.’ We ensure that we comply with the legal requirements by following the RE Today curriculum for Religious Education and Understanding Christianity and, as such, parents have the right to withdraw.
At Willowbrook, we adapt the scheme and marry it with Acorn pedagogy enabling us to provide a detailed curriculum that allows for granularity, ensures high expectations are met with rich connections between learning. Our carefully sequenced units of work encompass prior learning, key knowledge, vocabulary, and skills. Our RE curriculum is successfully adapted, designed and developed for pupils with special educational needs and/or disabilities by the teacher as necessary. It is a curriculum that is broad, balanced and inclusive for all pupils.
In line with the RE OSFTED review, each Key Stage allows children to:
Build ‘substantive’ knowledge about various religious and non-religious traditions.
Investigate the beliefs and practices of religions and other world views
Investigate how religions and other world views address questions of meaning, purpose, and value
Investigate how religions and other world views influence morality, identity, and diversity.
Learn ‘how to know’ about religion and non-religion.
Build an awareness of their own presuppositions and values about what they study.
At Willowbrook, we are setting children up to make a smooth transition to secondary. Using our chosen curriculum, and holding children to account for their own active learning, we are enabling children’s critical thinking skills to be developed, their motivation to learn increased, and their knowledge and understanding of, and empathy with people and their beliefs, religious or otherwise, will be enhanced. The sequence of lessons ensures subject knowledge, depth and builds on prior learning.
Impact
Willowbrook pupils enjoy RE, and it has a good profile in the curriculum with weekly lessons for all age groups, Songs of Worship featuring in singing assemblies, and regular RE focussed assemblies. Children develop a broad and balanced understanding of the main religions at an age-appropriate level. This means that children are developing longer-term knowledge and understanding. They can make connections in their learning over time, relating what they have learned about different religious beliefs, people, festivals and events within religions, and between different religions.

Ready, steady, GO!!! Sports Day news
It's Sport Day today. Gates will be open from 1pm for parents / carers to join us on the field.
For safeguarding reasons, children will be with their class on one side of the track alongside their teachers - parents / carers will be asked to stay on the other.
Children are asked to wear their PE kit to school - they may, if you wish wear their house colour - however all children are welcome to wear a white top - we do not want you to go out and buy anything.
The PTA will be on site providing refreshments - please note, they can only accept cash.
Children will return to their classes at the end of the event & can be collected by parents/carers (or a family member/approved person if arranged prior to the event) - please collect from the outside door of their classroom.

Sports Day 2026
An unforgettable afternoon had by all.
The afternoon started with four Oak Class students leading a whole school warm up. Everyone at Willowbrook completed the three races – hurdles, egg and spoon, and the sprint. The Oak Class students handed out the placings.
Congratulations to this year’s winners, Dahl (yellow house) with 785 points.
Thank you to F.O.W.S. for making our sports day even better!
A big well done to Mrs Sutton for winning the teacher’s race.
A huge thank you to all who came to support their child/children and to those who joined in on the mums race, the dads race and the toddlers race. We can’t wait to see you again next year for another wonderful Sports Day here at Willowbrook.
Written by Paige in Year 5
